To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

foreign language programs are not well-positioned to take advantage of the internationalization trend in higher education, and that this is due to discontinuities and contradictions in their own discourses and practices.

foreign language departments are often marginalized in internationalization efforts, that they are not always aware of the potential of their programs to contribute to internationalization, that they are often not in contact with other units that have similar goals and could be natural partners in internationalization, and that they often lack the necessary tools and expertise to collaborate with other units.

(1) foreign language study has been and continues to be a key component in the internationalization process; (2) the internationalization of higher education has led to a marginalization of foreign languages in the United States and abroad; (3) the internationalization process is not a one-way street and is not limited to the United States and its institutions of higher education; (4) internationalization has been a global phenomenon, but the process has been more successful in some parts of the world than
In summary, our research is concerned with
how language departments are positioned within the internationalization of the curriculum.
how language departments can be repositioned to become an indispensible and central component of higher education internationalization.
the ways that the study of languages is connected to the study of the world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the internationalization and globalization of the university is not only a process, but also a discourse, and that the discursive practices that have been used to internationalize the university have been detrimental to foreign language departments.
language departments are not only important, but also indispensable in internationalization of higher education.
the foreign language departments have been separated from natural allies and that this separation has been caused by discontinuous discourses in the departments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the internationalization of U.S. universities is incomplete without foreign language study.
foreign languages are an essential part of international education and that international education can be enriched by the inclusion of language study.
foreign language departments should take advantage of the internationalization of higher education to reposition themselves as an indispensable partner in the global education of U.S. students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language departments can be a powerful partner for international and global studies departments and programs, but they must first reposition themselves as such.

foreign language study is a critical component of the internationalization of higher education, and that language departments are well positioned to contribute to internationalization in ways that are complementary to the goals and activities of international and global studies.
language departments are in a unique position to provide the skills and competencies that are essential for internationalization and globalization.
